Reproducing Pakhomov et al. (2023) from dandiset 001027¶

Paper. Pakhomov AG, Gudvangen E, Mangalanathan U, Kondratiev O, Redondo L, Semenov I (2023). Next generation CANCAN focusing for remote stimulation by nanosecond electric pulses. Bioelectrochemistry 152:108437. doi:10.1016/j.bioelechem.2023.108437. The claims file was written from the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC10247516), with its Methods and figure legends; the version of record is not open access, and there is no supplement or linked code.

Dandiset. DANDI:001027, version 0.240605.1859. The paper cites no version of the dandiset. This is the only published version, and the draft has the same ten assets and size (3,667,103,151 bytes) and was last modified when this version was published, so the most recent published version is pinned.

What the dandiset holds. Ten NWB files, one dish each, with one stitched 10x YO-PRO-1 image of a CHO monolayer after a pulse protocol in a quadrupole array: Packet 1 (3 dishes), Packet 2 (4) and Packet 3 (3), each rotated once from every electrode, first pulse 4 kV. This is the experiment of Figure 8. The single-cell time-lapse of Figure 4 and the monolayer experiments of Figures 5, 6, 7 and 9 are not in it.

Claim Tested here

The helper module cancan.py streams the files, finds the electrodes and measures the ROI profiles; its docstring says where each parameter comes from.

In [1]:
import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import cancan

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
dishes = cancan.load_all()
for d in dishes:
    d["electrodes"] = cancan.find_electrodes(d["img"], d["valid"])
    d["background"], d["background_each"] = cancan.background(d["img"], d["electrodes"])
print(f"loaded {len(dishes)} files from dandiset {cancan.DANDISET_ID} version {cancan.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

loaded 10 files from dandiset 001027 version 0.240605.1859 in 246 s

Data check¶

What was loaded, and each check of the metadata against the values. The files hold one image each and no time series, so there is no trial table or clock to align; the check that the data streams share a clock does not apply.

One of the session descriptions in full:
  2. Experiments were conducted in a 4 electrodes setup. CanCan protocol applied at 4.0kV (first pulse) with the subsequent canceling pulses 12.5% lower than pulses before. Packets were repeated 1 times at 1Hz frequency. Than also at 1Hz frequency protocol was shifted and than electrode 2 was starting electrode with noted amplitude of the first pulse. Protocol finished when all 4 electrodes were active pulse electrodes. Protocol2 had 8 phases of pulses, 600ns pulse duration, canceling pulses delivered without delay. Detailed information on pulsing parameters, electrodes and procedures can be found in 10.1016/j.bioelechem.2023.108437.

Every description names a first pulse of 4.0 kV and one rotation (one packet from each electrode), as the Figure 8 legend says, and the packet counts (3, 4, 3) fit its n = 3-4. The descriptions define Protocol 1 as 4 phases, Protocol 2 as 8 phases without delay and Protocol 3 as 8 phases with 5-us delays, as the paper defines Packets 1, 2 and 3 (Section 2.3).

Largest correlation between two different dishes' images: 0.864
Any two reduced images identical: False

The ten files are distinct recordings: no two digests or images are identical (the largest correlation between two dishes' reduced images is 0.86). The image unit is "n.a." and the resolution field is 96 in nine files and 1.0 in dish 10, neither a pixel size, so the files do not give the scale of the image. The subject is a dish of the CHO cell line, and the species identifier NCBITaxon 10029 is Cricetulus griseus, the Chinese hamster; the dandiset's summary names it as "Cricetulus griseus - Cricetulus aureus". The age "P1D" has no meaning for a cell line. Nine files name the ORCA-Flash4.0 camera and a 10x objective (Methods: "10x, 0.38 NA"; the files say NA 0.40); dish 10 names no device, and its session starts on 18 March at 18:50, the evening after the other Packet 2 and 3 dishes.

Center-to-center diagonal 5.27 to 5.53 mm; edge-to-edge 3.41 to 3.66 mm; footprints 1.59 to 2.04 mm across (needles 1.5 mm, Methods 2.3).
Paper: ROIs cover +/-1.65 mm (small array) or +/-3.65 mm (large array, 8.4-mm diagonal), excluding <5% of the diagonal next to the electrodes.

The image is stitched from tiles. In the three dishes shown, the left edge of the imaged area steps at rows 1840 to 1848 pixels apart or twice that (3688), as tiles about 1844 pixels tall would make it; one step in each of them is 5736 pixels, which is not a multiple of that spacing, and dish 10 has steps of 1632 and 2048 in place of the second step of 3688 in the other two. A spacing of about 1844 pixels is about 90% of the camera's 2048, which is consistent with unbinned tiles overlapping by 10% and not resampled, and so with 0.65 um per pixel. At that scale the electrode footprints are 1.6 to 2.0 mm across, a little wider than the 1.5-mm needles, as a crushed or unexposed rim would make them. The arrays are the small one: the edge-to-edge diagonal is about 3.5 mm, and 5% short of each electrode leaves about 1.6 mm from the center, which is the +/-1.65 mm span the Methods give for the small array. The large array (8.4-mm diagonal) would need a scale about 2.4 times larger, and its footprints would then be about 4.5 mm across, three times the needle. The scale is consistent with the data but is not stated in them, so the ROIs are also placed by a rule that needs no scale (rel, below).

bgt = pd.DataFrame([{"dish": d["subject_id"], "packet": d["packet"], "date": d["session_start"][:10],
                     "background_mean": round(d["background"], 1),
                     "background_per_electrode": np.round(d["background_each"], 1).tolist()} for d in dishes])
print("Median intensity inside each electrode footprint (central 60% of the radius), raw counts:")
print(bgt.sort_values(["packet", "dish"]).to_string(index=False))
print("\nBy imaging date:")
print(bgt.groupby("date").background_mean.agg(["count", "mean", "min", "max"]).round(1).to_string())

# Saturation within the ROI strip of each dish (the main ROI geometry), from the per-block fraction.
rows = []
for d in dishes:
    e = d["electrodes"]; c = np.array([(a, b) for a, b, _ in e]); cen = c.mean(0)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[:d["img"].shape[0], :d["img"].shape[1]]
    half = cancan.HALF_SPAN_MM * 1000 / cancan.UM_PER_PX / cancan.BLOCK
    mask = np.zeros(d["img"].shape, bool)
    for i, j in [(0, 2), (1, 3)]:
        u = (c[j] - c[i]) / np.hypot(*(c[j] - c[i])); nrm = np.array([-u[1], u[0]])
        along = (yy - cen[0]) * u[0] + (xx - cen[1]) * u[1]
        across = (yy - cen[0]) * nrm[0] + (xx - cen[1]) * nrm[1]
        mask |= (np.abs(along) <= half) & (np.abs(across) <= half / 46)
    rows.append({"dish": d["subject_id"], "saturated_frac_in_rois": float(d["saturated"][mask].mean()),
                 "saturated_frac_image": float(d["saturated"].mean())})
sat = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nFraction of pixels >= 65000 (of 65535):")
print(sat.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.2e}"))

The footprints' interior is the only region of each image where cells were not exposed, and the files hold no sham dish or cell-free region, so it serves as the background in the background-subtracted reading. The intensity there is about twice as high in the three Packet 1 dishes (imaged on 24 March 2021) as in the seven others (17 and 18 March), so the a.u. scale differs between imaging days. The files do not record exposure or gain. Saturated pixels are too few to affect an ROI mean.

Each panel spans 1800 x 1800 blocks around the array center; every electrode lies inside it.

Profiles under every reading¶

The paper gives the span and number of ROIs but leaves open the details below, which the claims file names or which the Methods leave open (author, step 1.6). Each is run both or all ways:

  • geom: ROIs cover +/-1.65 mm from the geometrical center at 0.65 um per pixel (abs; Methods 2.4), or run to 5% of the edge-to-edge diagonal short of each electrode footprint (rel; Methods 2.4, "<5% of the diagonal length"), which needs no scale.
  • n_per_diag: "92 ... ROI, placed along one or both diagonals" (Methods 2.4) read as 46 per diagonal (92 over both) or 92 per diagonal.
  • center: the mean of the two ROIs flanking 0, or one ROI centered at 0 (claims file).
  • diag: the mean of both diagonals, or one (d1, E0 to E2; d2, E1 to E3). Which electrode is e1 is not in the files, so d1 and d2 are both run for "one diagonal".
  • bg: intensities as recorded, or less the per-dish background inside the electrode footprints. The Methods say nothing of a background for monolayers (Section 2.2 subtracts one for single cells).

The main reading, used for the measured values, is abs, 46 per diagonal, flank, both, raw: the stated span and ROI count, both diagonals as Figure 5B averages them, and the a.u. values as recorded, as the claims file says they are judged.

Most dishes show the shape of their group's mean profile. The Protocol 3 dishes peak broadly at the center (about 400 to 470 a.u. raw) and are lowest toward the electrodes, with narrow spikes above this in dish 03 near one end (its maximum, 561.3 a.u.) and in dish 11 at about -0.2 mm (its maximum, 548.0 a.u.) and at about +0.6 mm. Protocol 2 dishes 12, 13 and 14 are highest at the electrode ends (maxima 543.5 to 586.6 a.u. raw), with a lower central peak. Protocol 2 dish 2 is the exception: it is highest at one end (437.0 a.u.), but its other end (about 290 to 325 a.u.) is below its center (about 400), and its normalized center is 105.9% raw and 112.3% with the background subtracted (cell above), against 63.3 to 84.4% raw in the other three Protocol 2 dishes. Even so, every Protocol 3 dish (125.0 to 137.0% raw) is above every Protocol 2 dish, so the group difference does not rest on one dish. The Protocol 1 dishes are high at both ends and in the center, and dish 20 is lower than the other two on one side. Subtracting each dish's background shifts the curves and keeps these shapes.

fig8a-equal-center-uptake¶

Packets 1, 2 and 3 (4 kV, 1Px4) produce the same YP uptake in the center of the array, 215 to 235 a.u. (Results, 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 8A)

Criterion: the mean over dishes of the center ROI per packet, in a.u., each within 193.5 to 258.5 a.u.; no pair of packets differs by a two-sided Student's t-test at p < 0.05. Reproduced when both hold; partially reproduced when no pair differs but a value is out of range.

In [10]:
def ttest(a, b):
    return stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=True)

def center_outcome(g, labels):
    vals = {p: g[g.packet == q].center_au.values for p, q in labels.items()}
    means = {p: v.mean() for p, v in vals.items()}
    in_range = {p: 193.5 <= m <= 258.5 for p, m in means.items()}
    ps = {f"{a}v{b}": ttest(vals[a], vals[b]).pvalue for a, b in [(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)]}
    differ = any(p < 0.05 for p in ps.values())
    out = "reproduced" if all(in_range.values()) and not differ else (
        "partially_reproduced" if not differ else "not_reproduced")
    return {**{f"P{p}_center": round(m, 1) for p, m in means.items()},
            **{f"p_{k}": float(f"{v:.3g}") for k, v in ps.items()}, "outcome": out}

Result: not reproduced. Under the main reading the center means are 648.7 a.u. (Packet 1), 388.5 (Packet 2) and 383.4 (Packet 3), none within 193.5 to 258.5, and Packet 1 differs from Packets 2 and 3 (p = 0.00044 and 0.00093). All 48 readings give not reproduced: Packet 1 is 332.5 to 381.1 a.u. even with the background subtracted, and its p-values against the other two stay below 0.05 (largest 0.047 and 0.026). Packets 2 and 3 do not differ in any reading (smallest p 0.174); with the background subtracted they are 213.4 to 225.2 and 171.5 to 232.8 a.u. The Packet 1 dishes were imaged on another day with a background about twice as high (mean 308.1 a.u., against 161.8 for the dishes of 17 March and 150.3 for that of 18 March); as a ratio to each dish's own background the centers are 2.11, 2.37 and 2.50, and only Packet 1 against Packet 3 differs (p = 0.047). That ratio is not the paper's measure and does not decide the outcome.

fig8a-more-uptake-near-electrodes¶

Packets 1 and 3 cause much more YP uptake near the electrodes (250 to 350 a.u.) than Packet 2 (about 120 a.u.), p < 0.01. (Results, 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 8A)

Criterion: near the electrodes is the most peripheral ROI; readings (a) the mean of the ROIs closest to each electrode, (b) the ROI closest to e1; one diagonal or both. Reproduced when, under one reading, Packets 1 and 3 lie in 225 to 385 a.u., Packet 2 in 108 to 132 a.u., and each of Packets 1 and 3 exceeds Packet 2 by a two-sided Student's t-test at p < 0.01; partially reproduced when the tests hold and the values do not. The files do not say which electrode is e1, so reading (b) is run below in three ways: with each image label as e1 in every dish, with the end most favourable to the claim in each dish, and over every assignment of e1.

In [12]:
def near_outcome(g, labels):
    vals = {p: g[g.packet == q].periph_au.values for p, q in labels.items()}
    means = {p: v.mean() for p, v in vals.items()}
    rng = {1: (225, 385), 2: (108, 132), 3: (225, 385)}
    in_range = all(rng[p][0] <= means[p] <= rng[p][1] for p in (1, 2, 3))
    t13 = {p: ttest(vals[p], vals[2]) for p in (1, 3)}
    tests = all(t13[p].pvalue < 0.01 and t13[p].statistic > 0 for p in (1, 3))
    out = "reproduced" if (in_range and tests) else ("partially_reproduced" if tests else "not_reproduced")
    return {**{f"P{p}_periph": round(m, 1) for p, m in means.items()},
            "t_1v2": round(t13[1].statistic, 2), "p_1v2": float(f"{t13[1].pvalue:.3g}"),
            "t_3v2": round(t13[3].statistic, 2), "p_3v2": float(f"{t13[3].pvalue:.3g}"), "outcome": out}

# Reading (b): the ROI next to e1. The files do not say which electrode is e1, and E0 to E3 are
# assigned by angle in each image, so two versions are run: (i) the same label E0, E1, E2 or E3
# taken as e1 in every dish; (ii) a bound, taking in each dish the end most favourable to the
# claim (the lowest end in each Packet 2 dish, the highest in each Packet 1 and Packet 3 dish).
# The center is the mean of both diagonals, or the center of e1's own diagonal (E0, E2 on d1).
e_rows = []
for sid, p, bgv, pr_ in profs:
    for (geom, n, center), pr in pr_.items():
        sv = cancan.summary_values(pr, roi_at_zero=center == "at0")
        for b in ("raw", "bgsub"):
            off = bgv if b == "bgsub" else 0.0
            for k in range(4):
                for cdiag in ("both", "own"):
                    c = ((sv["center_d1"] + sv["center_d2"]) / 2 if cdiag == "both"
                         else sv["center_d1"] if k in (0, 2) else sv["center_d2"])
                    e_rows.append({"dish": sid, "packet": p, "geom": geom, "n_per_diag": n, "center": center,
                                   "bg": b, "cdiag": cdiag, "e1": f"E{k}", "center_au": c - off,
                                   "periph_au": sv[f"end_e{k}"] - off})
E1 = pd.DataFrame(e_rows); E1["pct"] = 100 * E1.center_au / E1.periph_au
ekeys = ["geom", "n_per_diag", "center", "bg", "cdiag"]

def favourable(df, col, low_for):
    """Per dish and reading, the e1 row with the lowest `col` in packets `low_for`, else the highest."""
    idx = [g[col].idxmin() if g.packet.iloc[0] in low_for else g[col].idxmax()
           for _, g in df.groupby(ekeys + ["dish"])]
    return df.loc[idx]

n_e1 = E1[E1.cdiag == "both"].groupby(ekeys + ["e1"]).apply(lambda g: pd.Series(near_outcome(g, AS_GIVEN))).reset_index()
print("(i) Same label as e1 in every dish:", len(n_e1), "readings")
print(n_e1.outcome.value_counts().to_string())
print("Readings with Packet 3 above Packet 2:", int((n_e1.P3_periph > n_e1.P2_periph).sum()), "of", len(n_e1))
print("Main geometry, raw:")
print(n_e1[(n_e1.geom == "abs") & (n_e1.n_per_diag == 46) & (n_e1.center == "flank") & (n_e1.bg == "raw")].to_string(index=False))
fav = favourable(E1[E1.cdiag == "both"], "periph_au", low_for={2})
n_fav = fav.groupby(ekeys).apply(lambda g: pd.Series(near_outcome(g, AS_GIVEN))).reset_index()
print("\n(ii) Most favourable end in each dish:", len(n_fav), "readings")
print(n_fav.outcome.value_counts().to_string())
print("Readings with Packet 3 above Packet 2:", int((n_fav.P3_periph > n_fav.P2_periph).sum()), "of", len(n_fav))
print("t (Packet 3 minus Packet 2):", n_fav.t_3v2.min(), "to", n_fav.t_3v2.max(), "; Packet 2 range (a.u.):",
      n_fav.P2_periph.min(), "to", n_fav.P2_periph.max())
print(n_fav.to_string(index=False))

# (iii) Every assignment of e1 to one of the four electrodes in each dish (4^10 = 1,048,576), with
# the two-sided Student's t-tests computed for each assignment.
import itertools
combos = np.array(list(itertools.product(range(4), repeat=10)), dtype=np.int8)

def t_equal_var(a, b):
    na, nb_ = a.shape[1], b.shape[1]
    sp = ((na - 1) * a.var(1, ddof=1) + (nb_ - 1) * b.var(1, ddof=1)) / (na + nb_ - 2)
    t = (a.mean(1) - b.mean(1)) / np.sqrt(sp * (1 / na + 1 / nb_))
    return t, 2 * stats.t.sf(np.abs(t), na + nb_ - 2)

n_enum = []
for key, g in E1[E1.cdiag == "both"].groupby(ekeys):
    g = g.sort_values(["packet", "dish", "e1"])
    pk = g.drop_duplicates("dish").packet.values
    Pe = g.periph_au.values.reshape(10, 4)[np.arange(10), combos].astype(float)
    v = {p: Pe[:, pk == p] for p in (1, 2, 3)}
    tests = np.ones(len(combos), bool)
    for p in (1, 3):
        t, pv = t_equal_var(v[p], v[2]); tests &= (t > 0) & (pv < 0.01)
    rng = {1: (225, 385), 2: (108, 132), 3: (225, 385)}
    inr = np.all([(rng[p][0] <= v[p].mean(1)) & (v[p].mean(1) <= rng[p][1]) for p in (1, 2, 3)], axis=0)
    n_enum.append({**dict(zip(ekeys, key)), "frac_reproduced": (tests & inr).mean(), "frac_partial": (tests & ~inr).mean(),
                   "frac_P3_above_P2": (v[3].mean(1) > v[2].mean(1)).mean()})
n_enum = pd.DataFrame(n_enum)
print("\n(iii) All", len(combos), "assignments of e1, in", len(n_enum), "readings:")
print(n_enum.round(4).to_string(index=False))

Result: not reproduced. Near the electrodes the Protocol 3 files show the least uptake, where the claim has Packet 3 above Packet 2: under the main reading 806.9 a.u. (Packet 1), 480.9 (Packet 2) and 296.2 (Packet 3), with Packet 3 below Packet 2 (t = -3.88, p = 0.012). Packet 3 is below Packet 2 in all 48 readings (t from -5.3 to -1.84). Packet 1 exceeds Packet 2 in every reading (t from 1.61 to 10.35, p from 0.00015 to 0.168).

Reading (b), the ROI next to e1, cannot be decided, as the files do not say which electrode is e1. Taking the same image label as e1 in every dish gives not reproduced in all 64 readings, with Packet 3 below Packet 2 in each. Taking in each dish the end most favourable to the claim (the lowest end of each Packet 2 dish, the highest of each Packet 1 and 3 dish) still gives not reproduced in all 16 readings: Packet 2 is 166.6 to 377.5 a.u., never in 108 to 132, and Packet 3 is not above Packet 2 by the test (t from -0.5 to 0.71). Over all 1,048,576 assignments of e1 to the four electrodes of each dish, none gives reproduced or partially reproduced, and at most 0.35% put the Packet 3 mean above the Packet 2 mean. No choice of e1 reproduces the claim, even in part.

fig8b-packet2-best-targeting¶

Normalized to the most peripheral ROI, YP emission in the center is 183% for Packet 2 and drops to 83% for Packet 3 and 74% for Packet 1. (Results, 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 8B)

Criterion: normalization per profile to its most peripheral ROI; readings (a) normalize each dish then average, (b) normalize the mean profile; peripheral ROI and diagonals as in the previous claim. Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance (164.7 to 201.3%, 74.7 to 91.3%, 66.6 to 81.4%) under one reading; partially reproduced when Packet 2 is the highest and above 100% while Packets 1 and 3 are below 100%, without all values in tolerance.

TOL = {2: (164.7, 201.3), 3: (74.7, 91.3), 1: (66.6, 81.4)}

def pct_outcome(g, labels, norm):
    v = {}
    for p, q in labels.items():
        s = g[g.packet == q]
        v[p] = s.pct.mean() if norm == "per_dish" else 100 * s.center_au.mean() / s.periph_au.mean()
    allin = all(TOL[p][0] <= v[p] <= TOL[p][1] for p in (1, 2, 3))
    partial = v[2] > max(v[1], v[3]) and v[2] > 100 and v[1] < 100 and v[3] < 100
    out = "reproduced" if allin else ("partially_reproduced" if partial else "not_reproduced")
    return {"P1_pct": round(v[1], 1), "P2_pct": round(v[2], 1), "P3_pct": round(v[3], 1), "outcome": out}

Result: not reproduced. Under the main reading the normalized centers are 81.3% (Packet 1), 82.8% (Packet 2) and 129.4% (Packet 3), where the claim has 74, 183 and 83%. Packet 3, not Packet 2, has the highest normalized center in all 96 readings, and Packet 2 is 52.5 to 123.7%. Per dish, the Protocol 3 files exceed the Protocol 2 files (t = 4.25, p = 0.008).

Reading (b), normalizing to the ROI next to e1, cannot be decided, as the files do not say which electrode is e1. The same image label as e1 in every dish gives not reproduced in all 256 readings. Choosing e1 in each dish to suit the claim (the lowest end in each Packet 2 dish, the highest in each Packet 1 and 3 dish) gives partially reproduced in 27 of 64 readings, all with 92 ROIs per diagonal, where a single end ROI is narrow and noisy; with the background subtracted, an end ROI near the background level makes a per-dish percentage unstable (Packet 2 from -661.8 to 572.3%). Over all 1,048,576 assignments of e1 to the four electrodes of each dish, none gives reproduced, none gives partially reproduced with 46 ROIs per diagonal, and at most 1.5% do with 92. The outcome is decided by reading (a), which can be run; that a small share of the possible e1 assignments meets the partial condition is recorded, not taken as the outcome.

Variant: Protocol 2 and Protocol 3 exchanged¶

The files labelled Protocol 3 (8 phases with 5-us delays) show the profile the paper reports for Packet 2, and the reverse. This variant reruns the three criteria with Packet 2 read from the Protocol 3 files and Packet 3 from the Protocol 2 files. It does not decide any outcome: the outcomes above test the dataset as labelled.

In the main geometry the normalized centers are 70.2, 162.3 and 76.4% (Packets 1, 2, 3) with the background subtracted and 81.3, 129.4 and 82.8% raw, so fig8b-packet2-best-targeting would be partially reproduced in 92 of 96 readings and reproduced in 2. fig8a-more-uptake-near-electrodes would still not be reproduced in 43 of 48 readings (with the background subtracted, Packet 1 is 498.8 a.u., above 385, and Packet 3 over Packet 2 gives p = 0.029, not below 0.01), and fig8a-equal-center-uptake in all 48, as Packet 1 is unchanged. A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper measured ROIs by hand in MetaMorph on the full-resolution images; here the electrodes are found automatically, ROIs are squares placed along both diagonals of the reduced image (8 x 8 pixel means), and the scale of 0.65 um per pixel is taken from the camera and objective, as the files give none. The ROI size, whether a background was subtracted, which diagonal, and which ROI is the center are not given by the paper; each is run every way, and no outcome depends on them. Reading (b) of the last two claims, the ROI next to e1, cannot be decided, as the files do not identify e1; it was run with each electrode label as e1 and with every assignment of e1, and no assignment reproduces either claim, though at most 1.5% of the assignments give fig8b-packet2-best-targeting the partial condition when 92 ROIs are placed per diagonal.

Two points are unresolved. First, the fig8a-equal-center-uptake failure rests largely on the Packet 1 dishes, which were imaged on another day with about twice the background of the others; a gain or exposure difference would scale all values and would not be removed by subtracting a background, and as a ratio to each dish's background Packet 1 does not differ from Packet 2 (p = 0.27) and differs from Packet 3 at p = 0.047. The files record no exposure or gain, so this cannot be settled. Second, the files labelled Protocol 2 and 3 behave as the paper's Packets 3 and 2. Each file's description defines the protocols as the paper defines the packets, so the data are tested as labelled, but a labelling error in the deposit or in the figure cannot be excluded.

What was found about the dataset. It holds only the Figure 8 experiment (10 dishes), not the single-cell time-lapse of Figure 4 or the monolayer experiments of Figures 5, 6, 7 and 9. The files labelled Protocol 3 (8 phases with 5-us delays) show the strongest central focusing and the least uptake near the electrodes, which the paper reports for Packet 2 (8 phases without delays), and the files labelled Protocol 2 behave as the paper's Packet 3; either the labels or the paper's assignment appear exchanged. The files give no pixel size (resolution 96, or 1.0 in dish 10), no position or identity of the electrodes, and no exposure or gain, and the Packet 1 dishes, imaged on another day, have about twice the background of the others. Dish 10 names no device. The species summary names two species for one cell line, and the age (P1D) does not apply to a cell line.
